speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand what's going on, can you tell me how long you've had these symptoms and if they started at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) arthritis.

Based on your history of a recent camping trip in Minnesota, a self-resolving knee pain (likely migratory arthritis), and current wrist swelling with systemic symptoms like fever and chills, this presentation is highly suggestive of Lyme arthritis. Can you confirm if the skin lesions you mentioned are specifically on your wrists, knees, or trunk?

REQUEST TEST: Erythromycin sensitivity test (to rule out other causes) and Erythema Chronicum Migrans history confirmation.
REQUEST TEST: Serology for Borrelia burgdorferi.
